newsitem.title: UK: Cuba still popular origin on sugar freight market.
newsitem.headline: Cuba still popular origin on sugar freight market.

text.p: Demand for Cuban sugar remained in evidence on the freight market on Thursday as orders and fixtures emerged from at least three charterers, shipbrokers said.

Sucre Export quoted for 13/14,000 tonnes in bags from north Continent to Mediterranean/Black Sea for early March and was also said to have fixed a prompt 14,000 tonnes in bulk from Cuba to the Black Sea at around $30.
Louis Dreyfus fixed 14,000 tonnes of Cuban sugar on the same run for February 20/25 at around the same rate.
Lorico was open for 13,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Cuba to Syria for 10/15 March and Genoc quoted for a prompt 7,000-tonne bagged cargo from Dunkirk to Hodeidah.
Other firmer business included Andre with a 10,000-tonne bagged parcel from Acajutla to east/west coast Africa option Black Sea. The rate has yet to emerge.
Shipbrokers said Cargill fixed 13,300/14,700 tonnes of bagged sugar from north Continent to Tunisia for prompt dates but no more details were available.
Sofracom fixed 12,000 tonnes of bulk sugar on its usual run from Reunion to Marseilles for the first half of March at approximately $28, they said.
In other news, the state-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp said it had completed a contract to buy 30,000 tonnes of sugar from Czarnikow at a private tender in New York.
Pricing details are confidential by mutual agreement but shipment is scheduled from April 20 to May 5.
